text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — GCP marketplace metering shows ~18% fewer usage units for customer ACME in last 24h vs our internal collector. noticing pattern around 00:00-01:30 UTC.
Monica Patel: ugh. are we comparing the same timezones/windowing?
Alex Chen: yes, both are UTC. I pulled raw exports: our collector has 1,240k units, GCP shows 1,018k.
Rajiv Kumar: can you paste a sample of the marketplace payload? sometimes the payload schema changed and our ingestion drops fields.
Alex Chen: here is a single webhook we got from GCP (redacted):
```
{
  "customer_id": "ACME_CORP",
  "usage": [{"timestamp": "2026-03-20T00:05:12Z", "units": 120}, {"timestamp": "2026-03-20T00:10:00Z", "units": 130}],
  "aggregation_id": "agg-20260320-0005",
  "plan": "dedicated-basic"
}
```
Monica Patel: thanks. our collector expects `start_ts`/`end_ts` fields in batch uploads — GCP is sending per-event items. that could cause our batch-merge to miss overlap dedup.
GCP Marketplace Bot: webhook delivery status: 5 failed deliveries to /integrations/gcp/metering between 2026-03-20T00:14Z and 2026-03-20T00:22Z. HTTP 429 then 502.
Sofia (billing): re: failures — do we have retry/backoff logs? if we dropped retries we could be missing whole windows.
Alex Chen: yes, our infra shows a backpressure policy that drops if queue > 200k and retry window > 5m. I found entries like: `dropped_msg_count=4321 reason=queue_full`.
Rajiv Kumar: other angle: aggregation_id pattern changed? we dedupe by (customer_id, aggregation_id). if GCP switched to ephemeral agg ids per-submission we'll double-count on our side or miss depending on merge.
Alex Chen: good call — I just grepped recent payloads, and there are now 2 different `aggregation_id` prefixes from the same account: `agg-20260320-0005` and `batch-20260320-a`. looks like they rolled a new batching pipeline.
Monica Patel: ok plan: 1) pull full webhook archive for ACME during 00:00-02:00 UTC (Alex) 2) export GCP marketplace usage CSV for same window (Sofia) 3) run local reconciliation script with 2 dedupe strategies (Raj).
Sofia (billing): exporting now. ETA ~15m. I'll include marketplace report + invoice linkage file.
Alex Chen: ran quick diff locally. with dedupe by `aggregation_id` we reproduce GCP numbers. with time-window bucketing we reproduce internal collector. sounds like two different canonical aggregation semantics.
Rajiv Kumar: thanks. can you paste the reconciliation SQL you used?
Alex Chen: sure — snippet: `SELECT customer_id, SUM(units) FROM usage_events GROUP BY customer_id, floor(extract(epoch FROM timestamp)/300)` — that buckets into 5m windows (our collector). if GCP is pre-aggregating per-batch, their units are already summed.
Monica Patel: hypothesis: GCP changed to pre-aggregated batches, but vendored marketplace adapter still sends per-event items + aggregation_id that differs across retries. result: our 5m bucket dedupe double-counts some batches as separate events.
Sofia (billing): I'll open a partner ticket with GCP marketplace ops and attach the sample payloads + failure logs. want me to cc engineering?
Rajiv Kumar: yes please cc eng-partnerships and eng-billing. also request their new payload schema doc and whether they guarantee idempotent `aggregation_id` across retries.
Alex Chen: added tasks: create a short-term reconciliation job to prefer aggregation_id when present, and add metric to alert if >5% delta between internal and marketplace for a customer. I'll draft revertable change.
Monica Patel: +1. also add test vectors to our ingestion harness with both `agg-` and `batch-` prefixes.
Sofia (billing): ticket opened with GCP: TICKET-98765. summarizing: payload format change + transient webhook 429s => missing/duplicated units. GCP acked, will consult infra team and reply by EOD.
GCP Marketplace Bot: update: TICKET-98765 status changed to "triage" by marketplace-ops.
Alex Chen: great. follow-ups: Sofia will push their marketplace CSV when ready, Raj will run dedupe experiments, Monica will add ingestion tests. I'll create the alert.
Monica Patel: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
